sources.notes: Source: Poddar et al., Cureus 18(3):e104772 (2026), KIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha; retrospective sterile-body-fluid antibiogram, Jan 2021-Dec 2022. 2307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive); GPC 54%, S. aureus most common (92/291), MRSA 48.9%; K. pneumoniae top GNB (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19). All susceptibility data are presented ONLY as unlabeled bar charts (Fig 1 = Gram-positive: S. aureus, CONS, Enterococcus; Fig 2 = Gram-negative: K. pneumoniae, E. coli, Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp.) plus narrative sentences. There are NO numeric susceptibility tables. Method: rendered figure pages with PyMuPDF at 6x, calibrated the y-axis from detected tick-label centers (Fig 2: 0%=y1383, 100%=y368; Fig 1 baseline y1504), then extracted each bar's top and mid-bar color programmatically. Color->drug map validated by matching extracted values to the paper's own text (Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs 'imipenem 41%', gentamicin 41.5 vs 'aminoglycosides 41%', cotrimoxazole 36.8 vs '37.5%', ciprofloxacin 36.8 vs '38%'; E. coli ciprofloxacin 10.8 vs 'ciprofloxacin resistance high 90%'; Pseudomonas ceftazidime 20.9 vs '21%', ciprofloxacin 9.9 vs '10-11%'). Values are %
issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems' — i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).

sources.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2024, part A: Enterobacterales (chapter 2) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 3), plus isolation counts from chapter 1. 99,027 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Colistin figures are percent intermediate. CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens) and Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations); the two sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17 (E. faecalis and E. faecium are counted separately). Part B of the ICMR AMRSN 2024 annual report (merged by the lead with Part A, chapters 1 to 3): typhoidal Salmonella, diarrhoeal pathogens, staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (invasive, Table 8.3) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"). Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) are left out. Fungal tables print S, I/SDD and R; only S is recorded. Several fungal percentages are printed 0.1 above the count ratio (e.g. 17/18 printed 94.5); recorded as printed. Isolates come from tertiary care hospitals; the report says the data do not reflect community AMR (p5). The ICMR network report for 2024 (21 regional centres; 99,027 culture-positive isolates). Extracted in two parts by table chapter and merged; the transcribed national summary used before this is superseded.

Table II reports % SUSCEPTIBLE by centre; Table III reports % RESISTANT (n/N) split by ESBL-producer vs non-ESBL. I derived OVERALL susceptibility by pooling Table III ESBL + non-ESBL resistant counts per drug (s = 100 - pooled %R, from_R:true for all pooled cells). Colistin values taken directly from the printed overall figures in the Results text (E. coli 99% = 271/274; K. pneumoniae 98% = 229/234), not from R. CAVEAT: Table III denominators (e.g. 167+202=369 for E. coli, 98+126=224 for K. pneumoniae) exceed stated collection totals of 341/304, likely reflecting drug-specific tested subsets/classification; per-drug pooled %R is nevertheless computed directly from printed n/N. Individual per-centre susceptibility values are available in Table II if centre-level breakdown is preferred. ESBL prevalence context: CDT dete
